lines.hook: What if a virus worse than COVID hit... tomorrow?
lines.intro: Not a zombie movie. A real, fast spreading virus. Here's how it would actually play out, step by step.
lines.relate: Remember March 2020? Empty shelves, no toilet paper, and everyone suddenly baking bread? Now imagine something even faster.
lines.day1: Day one. One person gets sick in a busy city. It just feels like a bad cold, so they still go to work.
lines.week1: By the end of the week, it's on planes. Ten cities, three continents. And every sick person infects about three more.
lines.math: That sounds small, but it grows fast. Three becomes nine, nine becomes twenty seven, and after ten rounds, it's over fifty thousand people.
lines.week3: Week three. Hospitals fill up. Schools close, people work from home, and masks are back.
lines.twist: But here's the crazy part. We're much faster now. In 2020, scientists designed a vaccine just two days after the virus's code was shared. Today, the goal is a new vaccine in one hundred days.
lines.real: So could this really happen? It has before. In 1918, the flu infected about five hundred million people. That's a third of the world.
lines.end: But back then, there were no vaccines, no internet, and no intensive care units. This time, we'd spot it sooner and fight back faster.
lines.cta: So be honest... what would you stock up on first? Tell me in the comments.
